procedure.description: revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 37227 (revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement) with date of service 2026-02-17. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish limb-threatening ischemia or failure of supervised exercise therapy.

criteria.text: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcer, or gangrene, Rutherford 4 to 6); or lifestyle-limiting claudication (Rutherford 3) that has failed at least 12 weeks of supervised exercise therapy and optimal medical therapy.
Hemodynamic confirmation: ankle-brachial index 0.4 or less, toe pressure below 30 mmHg, or TcPO2 below 30 mmHg for limb-threatening ischemia (ankle-brachial index below 0.9 for claudication).
Imaging (duplex, CT angiography, or angiography) demonstrating a femoropopliteal stenosis of 50 percent or more, or an occlusion, amenable to endovascular treatment.
Optimal medical therapy documented: an antiplatelet agent, a statin, and smoking cessation or cessation counseling.

chart.text: Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Blood pressure check. 138 over 86 today, 141 over 81 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Right heel ulcer 2.2 by 1.4 centimeters, pale base, no granulation tissue after 10 weeks of weekly debridement and offloading. Pedal pulses not palpable.

68 year old woman referred by podiatry for the right leg. Diabetic 23 years, hypertension, prior coronary stent. Discussed endovascular versus bypass; endovascular first given the anatomy. Her history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Right heel ulcer for 3 months that will not heal despite offloading and weekly wound care, and rest pain in the right foot at night relieved by hanging it off the bed. Rutherford 5. On aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 80. Quit smoking 7 weeks ago after 44 years; counseled again today and offered nicotine replacement.
Arterial studies. Ankle-brachial index right 0.36, left 0.88. Right toe pressure 26 mmHg. Monophasic waveforms at the right popliteal and tibial levels.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 222, LDL 135, HDL 38, triglycerides 181. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

CT angiography with runoff: right superficial femoral artery occluded over 10 centimeters from the mid thigh to the adductor canal, reconstitution of the above-knee popliteal artery, two-vessel runoff via the anterior tibial and peroneal. Contralateral mild disease. Aortoiliac segments patent.
Vitamin D came back 16. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Back to review the imaging. Plan right superficial femoral artery recanalization with atherectomy and stent, outpatient. Risks reviewed including embolization and need for bypass. Vitals today 114 over 83, pulse 76.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Pre-procedure visit. Creatinine 1.4, hold metformin, hydration protocol. Consent signed.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
